title: Scout Motors Traveler & Terra
eyebrow: SCOUT MOTORS · TRAVELER SUV & TERRA PICKUP · REVEALED OCTOBER 2024
verdict: A boxy, body-on-frame 4x4 with a solid rear axle and lockers at both ends is exactly the kind of truck this site exists for. The catch is that it doesn't exist yet: as of October 2026, Scout is welding test bodies in South Carolina and says customer deliveries start in 2028.
hero_note: No freely licensed photos of the Traveler or Terra exist yet. We'll add some when they do.

paragraphs: The Scout name went quiet when the last [[scout/scout-ii|Scout II]] left Fort Wayne in 1980. Volkswagen Group came to own the trademark in early 2021, when its truck arm Traton acquired Navistar, the company International Harvester's truck business had become. In May 2022 Volkswagen said it would build electric pickups and SUVs in the United States under the Scout name. Scout Motors was founded on May 24, 2022, with former Volkswagen Group of America boss Scott Keogh as CEO. Everything on this page is as announced or reported. None of it has been driven by a customer.

story.heading: A FACTORY IN SOUTH CAROLINA
paragraphs: On March 3, 2023, Scout announced a $2 billion factory in Blythewood, South Carolina, on about 1,100 acres. It is designed to build up to 200,000 vehicles a year and to employ more than 4,000 people. Scout says its vehicles will be engineered in Detroit and built in South Carolina, and it opened an R&D center in Novi, Michigan. On November 12, 2025, it announced that its global headquarters would be in Charlotte, North Carolina.

Scout plans to sell directly rather than through franchised dealers. Its website promises retail stores in 16 metro areas, growing to about 100 locations in the US and Canada by 2032. That plan has drawn lawsuits: the National Automobile Dealers Association sued Volkswagen Group and Scout on February 3, 2025, and Volkswagen and Audi dealers in California and Florida filed similar suits.

story.heading: THE REVEAL
paragraphs: On October 24, 2024, at an event just outside Nashville, Scout revealed two concepts: the Traveler SUV and the Terra pickup. The specification read like an off-roader's wish list. Both use a body-on-frame platform with a solid rear axle, four-wheel drive with an electric drive unit on each axle, and front and rear mechanical locking differentials. Launch coverage also reported an 800-volt architecture, 35-inch tires, more than 10,000 lb of towing for the Terra and more than 7,000 lb for the Traveler, and nearly 2,000 lb of payload.

Scout offered two powertrains. The battery-electric versions are projected to reach up to 350 miles of range. The "Harvester" extended-range versions add a gasoline generator and are projected to reach 500 miles or more. Scout said entry prices would start under $60,000, and launch coverage quoted figures as low as $50,000 for the Traveler and $51,500 for the Terra with incentives available at the time. Reservations opened that evening for $100, fully refundable. At the November 2025 Los Angeles Auto Show, Scout showed refreshed concepts, with the Terra on 37-inch tires.

story.heading: THE WAIT
paragraphs: In February 2024 Scout was talking about production starting in 2026. At the reveal it said 2027, and its website still says "initial production targeted for 2027, subject to change." In February 2026 Der Spiegel reported that series production would slip to summer 2028. In March 2026 Keogh said, "I see that sometime in 2028." Electrive reported that Scout had about 160,000 reservations at the time, and that 87% of them chose the Harvester range-extender.

In April 2026 AutoForecast Solutions reported production dates of September 2028 for the Traveler and March 2030 for the Terra. Scout declined to comment on that report, saying only that it expects customers to begin taking delivery in 2028. The range-extender version will now come first. In July 2026 Scout welded its first test Traveler body at Blythewood. For now, the original [[scout/scout-80-800|Scout 80]] and the Scout II remain the only Scouts you can actually drive.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · WHAT "HARVESTER" MEANS
callout.title: The range-extender most buyers picked
paragraphs: Scout's Harvester models are still driven by electric motors, with an onboard gasoline generator to recharge the battery. Scout says they can be charged at electric charging stations and refueled with gasoline, and projects 500 miles of range or more.

According to Scout's CEO, buyers chose this version far more often than the pure electric one: 87% of the more than 160,000 reservation holders picked it. Jalopnik reported in April 2026 that packaging the generator under the floor has caused engineering problems and that towing could be cut by roughly half compared with the electric version. Keogh said Scout was working on "solutions." Nothing is final until Scout publishes production specifications.

faq.q: When can I actually buy one?
faq.a: Scout says it expects customers to begin taking delivery in 2028 (statement reported April 2026), though its reservation pages still say initial production is targeted for 2027. AutoForecast Solutions reported in April 2026 that Traveler production would start in September 2028 and Terra production in March 2030, and Scout declined to comment on those dates.

Scout says entry-model pricing is "expected to start under $60,000" for both the Traveler and the Terra (scoutmotors.com, checked October 2026). At the October 2024 launch, coverage quoted as low as $50,000 for the Traveler and $51,500 for the Terra with incentives available at the time. Scout says final pricing will be confirmed closer to production.

faq.q: EREV or BEV: what's the difference?
faq.a: The battery-electric version is projected at up to 350 miles of range. The Harvester extended-range version adds a gasoline generator and is projected at 500 miles or more. By March 2026, 87% of reservation holders had chosen the EREV, and Scout now plans to launch it first. Jalopnik reported in April 2026 that EREV towing may be roughly half that of the EV.

On paper, yes. Scout has announced body-on-frame construction, a solid rear axle, four-wheel drive, and front and rear mechanical locking differentials for both models. Launch coverage also mentioned a front sway-bar disconnect, about a foot of ground clearance and 3 feet of water fording, but treat those as reported, not confirmed.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: Unknown, because production specifications haven't been published. The concepts were shown on 35-inch tires (Traveler) and 37-inch tires on 18-inch wheels (Terra, November 2025 LA Auto Show).

At Scout's $2 billion Production Center in Blythewood, South Carolina, announced March 3, 2023. It's planned for up to 200,000 vehicles a year and more than 4,000 jobs. The first test Traveler body was welded there in July 2026.

Reservations cost $100, are fully refundable and are non-binding. They opened on October 24, 2024. Electrive reported about 160,000 reservations by March 2026, with about three-quarters for the Traveler.

faq.q: Will I buy it from a dealer?
faq.a: No. Scout plans to sell directly, and says retail stores will open in 16 metro areas and grow to about 100 locations in the US and Canada by 2032. Dealer groups, including the National Automobile Dealers Association (February 3, 2025), have sued over the direct-sales plan.

At launch in October 2024, coverage reported more than 10,000 lb for the Terra, more than 7,000 lb for the Traveler, and nearly 2,000 lb of payload for both. Scout says capacities vary by model and trim, and the EREV may tow less.

faq.q: Is it related to the original Scout?
faq.a: In name and styling only. Volkswagen Group acquired the Scout trademarks in 2021 through Navistar, and the new trucks borrow the original Scout's shape. Scout Motors now owns the Scout, Traveler, Terra and Travelall trademarks, and IH Parts America notes that it uses them under license for parts for the original trucks.
